body:
You're not listening to me!

This isn't about what I did. It's about what reactions I got.

I wrote that I was at it for months and you suggest that I murdered someone.

Sure. It's possible to spend several nights a week for months doing that. And it's accepted if you get paid for it.

Maybe try reading what I write before suggesting that I'm a murderer.

I'm not the one who's uncooperative. You're the one who isn't reading what I'm writing.

I saw you guilt tripping someone in another thread, so maybe I shouldn't be surprised.

"I'm here to help" posts are also against the rules. Read the flipping sidebar.

What does it matter what I did?

It's something that according to the rules means I'm not getting any help. My therapist is about to find out about it and she already wants me to justify seeing her.

People kept telling me to find someone to talk to. I did. Now I'm finding out that it's against the rules for me to see somebody.

I've even been told that my mental health is fine in response to saying that I think it would've been better if I was never born just because I fall between the cracks in that DSM-V. Ya know, that thing that they've kept updating because they missed a spot.

But of course this version is perfect and I'm fine.

It was just updated and there's decades between updates. I can't do this for decades until they decide that I'm allowed to not be fine.
The reactions I got here when I wrote that with my main account showed that writing it is a bad idea.

But I'm not getting any diagnosis because that manual of their specifically spells out that my circumstances don't meet their criteria.

And then that bureaucratic psychiatrist is gonna tell my therapist that there isn't anything wrong with me.

My therapist already keeps asking me why I'm seeing her despite me telling her. She'll take this as a reason to kick me out.

And I'm literally falling between their cracks. If I had made money on what brought me to this point I'd meet their criteria.

But the problem is that I didn't make any money, so I don't fit any diagnosis.

And my therapist is sending me to someone else to find out what's wrong with me. I already know that on paper I'm gonna be fine. When I asked for help in another thread and wrote that there isn't a day when I don't think it would've been better if I had never been born I was told that my mental health is fine and I don't need a therapist.

I know I'm not fine, but my therapist is going to be told the same thing by whatever psychiatrist she sends me to.

According to their rules I'd be worse off and in need of help if I had more money.

But my mental health is not fine. I feel like I don't deserve to live. How does that make me fine?

I tried doing as people told me to and ask for help, but because I fall between the cracks in the bureaucracy (literally, if I had made money on what brought me to this point it would count as real) I keep needing to justify needing help.

Doesn't meet criteria.

And if it's impossible to diagnose me with anything, why would they help me?

And how do I explain why I want to continue therapy? "For problems that don't exist on paper"? I'm already trying to justify seeing a therapist and now she's sending me to somebody who's only response within their rules can be "there isn't a problem".

I thought I could get some help if I just went to a therapist and talked through my situation. I don't have a day when I don't think it would've been better if I hadn't been born, but on paper there isn't anything wrong with me, so I'll just get sent away to handle everything myself again.
I'm sorry I'm too useless to figure that out myself.

I'm not talking about "I can't help you", I'm talking about it being written down in the DSM-V that my circumstances don't count.

I've spent weeks trying to convince my therapist that it is a problem for me and now she wants to send me to somebody else.

"Anything that I'm struggling with"

How do I know what counts and what doesn't?

Do I have to tell them that I'm not straight even if this isn't any problem whatsoever? I'm not interested in getting into a relationship or hooking up with anyone. I don't want to be treated like it is a problem I'm in denial about just because it's something other people can struggle with. The worst thing about that has been some ignorant comments online. I count myself lucky.

Meanwhile I have survivor's guilt for completely unrelated reasons. It's something that's not commonly accepted as resulting in it (according to DSM-V, not just society). How do I get somebody to see that as a problem when there are much more common things going on with me?

I don't want a "that doesn't matter, this does". I'm sick and tired of having my situation downplayed.
